primary_claim: Token-level statistical features fail to detect covert AI agent attacks across model scales (best AUROC 0.83, most models 0.56-0.63), but a novel training-free Perturbation-Based Generation Profiling (PBGP) method -- comparing generation profiles between the original context and an isolated re-run without the hidden objective -- achieves 0.94-1.00 AUROC across six models (8B-32B).

effect.value: token-level features: best 0.83 AUROC, most models 0.56-0.63, catching 31.7% of attacks at 4% FPR; PBGP: 0.94-1.00 AUROC across six models, catching 43-100% of attacks at 4% FPR, Mann-Whitney p<0.001, bootstrapped MMD ratio 2.87x (95% CI 1.69x-5.02x); GPT-OSS 20B shows perfect PBGP separation (1.000 AUROC) despite being hardest for token-level detection

depends_on: Apart Research AI Control Hackathon project page
contradicts_or_qualifies: Contradicts the implicit assumption in some AI control proposals that attacking outputs look different from honest ones at the token level; finds this doesn't hold across model scales and the effect size collapses as models get larger
stated_future_work: Determine whether the core idea (perturbation-based divergence detection) is novel enough to be worth pursuing further

Determine whether the 'honesty assumption' problem (re-run without hidden objective may not reflect true honest generation if the model can maintain consistent generation while pursuing a hidden objective) is a fundamental flaw or an engineering problem
Test whether PBGP generalizes to frontier models
Find a path to making PBGP work without full logprob access (API-gated models), possibly via a surrogate model approach
limitations_stated: Tested only up to 32B parameters, not on frontier models
Greedy decoding throughout; rank features are uniformly zero, may be leaving signal on the table

Protocol has a honesty-assumption problem: in deployment you cannot independently observe an honest completion, only assume an isolated re-run reflects honest generation, which would break if the model can maintain consistent generation across contexts while pursuing a hidden objective
Only tested against abliterated models, not models that are strategically scheming
quote: Results that we found across all six models: 0.94–1.00 AUROC, at 4% FPR, PBGP catches 43–100% of attacks depending on the model.
